name: Kim Hyo Dong

attribution.legal_posture: Two Member States designated the subject; this report carries no UN Committee designation. It carries Republic of Korea and UN Panel-reported Member State allegation context. This is an administrative sanctions designation, with legal posture limited to the administrative action.

caveats: Administrative sanctions designation; the record has no criminal charge or conviction.
Employment aliases may be stolen, borrowed, or synthetic identities; alias ownership and worker identity remain source-unresolved.
The claims were Member State information, and the Lao People’s Democratic Republic had not replied at publication.
The exact-ID bridge uses the same name, Tongmyong organization, Laos geography, and representative role across the ROK release and S/2023/656; sensitive appendix identifiers are excluded.
The forced-labor sentence applies across the action and collectively to the five footnoted IT-branch managers; person-specific adjudication requires a separate finding.
The individuals and company were designated by two Member States; the report attributes the designations to Member State action rather than the UN Committee.

statements: A Member State reported Tongmyong Technology Trade Company as a Laos-based Munitions Industry Department affiliate that dispatched IT workers; its reported representative was Kim Hyo Dong, while Yu Song Hyok and Yun Song Il reportedly arranged office space/accommodation and mediated with foreign brokers to cash out embezzled virtual assets.

sources.support: Supports Tongmyong Tech, the three reported support roles, office/accommodation assistance, virtual-asset cash-out mediation and no-reply status

The ROK joint release designates Kim Hyo Dong and names him as Tongmyong Technology Trade Company's representative and IT delegation leader in Laos; it collectively alleges labor-control practices by five footnoted IT-branch managers without separately proving every practice by each manager
